decisions.reason: The candidate's same-message INTRODUCE already fully records GPIO3-controlled LED power cutoff and the zero-standby-current target.
Switching the separate 5V rail does not change the standalone USB-powered 3.3V supply or its source-selection behavior.
The GPIO-switched downstream 5V rail does not alter the AXP2101 battery, USB, VMID, or VSYS power-path requirements.
The existing interface already carries 5V and 5V_EN; the source changes rail usage but does not change the connector, pinout, or pin-order requirement.
The switched 5V load decision has no effect on the battery connector's series, mounting, or unresolved pinout.
Placing the addressable LEDs on the GPIO3-switched 5V rail necessarily changes their previously stated 3.3V supply to 5V.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Doesn't the 5V_EN pin solve this? We can cut the entire 5V rail via GPIO3 when LEDs are not needed, dropping standby current to zero.

decisions.reason: The source changes power-rail control but does not change the sensor board's role of providing sensor connectors.
The switched supply does not change the separate LED board's role or its count of eight addressable LEDs.
The source decision concerns power control and does not alter component availability, cost, or sourcing policy.
The 5V rail shutdown behavior does not affect battery connector placement, orientation, clearance, or spacing.
The source does not change I2C speed, pull-ups, cable length, or series-resistor configuration.
The electrical rail-control decision does not alter any power-board mechanical layout constraint.
